newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Record dengue fever cases in Singapore in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Record dengue fever cases in Singapore in 1996.

text.p: A record 3,128 cases of dengue fever were reported in Singapore in 1996, the Straits Times newspaper said on Friday.
The daily quoted the Environment Ministry as saying three people died last year from the disease, which is carried by a species of mosquito called Aedes.
The previous highest annual total of dengue cases in Singapore was in 1992, when 2,878 cases were recorded, it said.

Dengue, also called breakbone fever, causes high temperatures, headaches and pain in muscles and joints. It is usually over in five to six days but can occur in a haemorrhagic form with internal bleeding.

The number of dengue cases has increased sharply over the last five years. Researchers blame the increase on population growth, the spread of urbanisation, deteriorating conditions in cities and the build-up of mosquito breeding sites. Some have suggested the rise may also be due to global warming.

Singapore has an active government programme to combat dengue and other mosquito-born diseases such as malaria. It has spent almost Singapore $4.7 million (US$3.33 million) in recent years on destroying breeding sites in public housing.
